title: Strong quarterly beat for MSFT: EPS of $7.78 vs $25.5 estimate. Revenue of $115.9B exceeded consensus. Management expressed confidence in full-year targets citing robust pipeline and strong demand trends.

Strong quarterly beat for AAPL: EPS of $2.95 vs $104.4 estimate. Revenue of $105.9B exceeded consensus. Management expressed confidence in full-year targets citing robust pipeline and strong demand trends.

GOOGL Q2 results disappointed investors as revenue declined 14.9% year-over-year. CEO warned of deteriorating conditions and cut guidance for next quarter. Operating margins contracted 121bps on cost pressures.
JPM delivered results largely in line with expectations. The company maintained its guidance range and flagged both opportunities and risks in the current environment. Operating margins stable.
AAPL delivered exceptional Q4 results with revenue growth of 12.6% year-over-year. CEO highlighted accelerating market share gains and raised forward guidance. Operating margins expanded 54bps.

Disappointing quarter for JNJ: missed on both top and bottom line. Revenue of $71.2B fell short of $70.7B consensus estimate. Margin pressure and inventory buildup weighed on results. Guidance lowered.

MSFT earnings miss: EPS of $2.47 vs $15.9 expected. Management cited geopolitical uncertainty, inflation headwinds, and demand weakness. Credit loss provisions increased $1.6B. Outlook remains cautious.
META delivered exceptional Q2 results with revenue growth of 23.1% year-over-year. CEO highlighted accelerating market share gains and raised forward guidance. Operating margins expanded 138bps.
GOOGL Q4 earnings call: CEO highlighted record free cash flow of $36.3B and announced dividend increase of 13%. New product launches driving accelerating growth in core markets. Guidance raised.
GS Q1 earnings call: CEO highlighted record free cash flow of $20.6B and announced dividend increase of 6%. New product launches driving accelerating growth in core markets. Guidance raised.
JNJ reported below-consensus earnings amid regulatory challenges and increased competition. The company announced restructuring affecting 5K employees and warned of continued near-term uncertainty.
JPM Q1 earnings: EPS of $5.26 in line with consensus estimate of $48.7. Revenue growth of 9.5% year-over-year consistent with guidance. No material changes to full-year outlook.
